as `trace_spacing`, plus the 2 oz pad mask-bridge check inside `physical_copper_gap`; that check runs on outer layers only (#8913) and judges a declared 2 oz outer weight only, otherwise reporting `physical_copper_gap_incomplete` at info. Reported, not reproduced (#9034): on one further 4-layer board (not committed) kct reported 19 errors against the fab's 6 danger + 1 warning; the surplus cause is unmeasured, but kct emits at most one finding per copper-source pair per layer (closest measurement wins -- measured on the #9034 fixture), so it cannot come from per-edge inflation within a pair. No fab-sourced edge justifies a threshold change, so the stricter same-net error stays (#8938). One narrow exception (#9420): two pads of the SAME footprint on one identical non-empty net in the 2 oz pad mask-bridge check report at info (still listed). Different footprints, different nets and every other pair keep the error. Zone-fill (pour) gaps are kct's own advisory only and report at info, not tiered: JLCDFM does not judge pour clearance -- 1,516 pour-to-pad gaps at 0.10-0.13 mm went unflagged on the #8938 board -- so kct's warning count for this category exceeds the fab's by that population by design.

`mask_to_copper` is default-on for an explicit --mfr `jlcpcb*` since #8842 (interim 0.09 mm danger / 0.15 mm warning); a bare `kct check` with no --mfr does not engage it, and the native path needs an unmodified saved source. Observed 5 danger, all same-net: a track running beside, along, or leaving and jogging beside its own pad at 0-0.08 mm (#8914); those shapes stay errors at the 0.09 mm band. Since #8858 one shape is `within_own_pad` at info: a straight track entering its own pad (plain, or custom since #9750) once, at 45 degrees or steeper, exposing nothing beyond the pad and leaving no more copper under mask beside the opening than that one crossing (or a track lying wholly on the pad). The fab did not flag plain entries (#8914; 655 entries on the consumer board, 0 flagged). On boards 00-07 (0 mm expansion) that was 963 of 1,542 errors. Pass-through, along-edge and straddling tracks, shallow entries, arcs, vias and pours touching the pad, expansion rings wider than the construction budget, and different-net copper keep their verdict. Since #9284 a second shape is `own_pour_thermal` at info: a plain pad tied to its own same-net pour by thermal spokes, as pcbnew declares and the fill shows, at 0 mm expansion with nothing beyond the pad, and within the 0.15 mm examined band only 1-4 spoke crossings (pour body farther out). JLCDFM listed no item for the four such pads on board 01 (relief gaps 0.2 and 0.3 mm; #8858, 2026-11-17); same-net pairs were absent, not rated Good. Unconnected same-net pour, a pour body inside 0.15 mm, and pour exposed by a positive expansion keep their verdict. Since #9436 a further shape is `own_pour_solid` at info: a plain pad whose effective zone connection is solid and whose fill shows the join, at 0 mm expansion with nothing beyond the pad. The consumer board had 13 such pads solid in their own-net pour; JLCDFM (`--mfr jlcpcb`, 2026-11-18) reported 0 danger / 0 warning for them. Since #9420 another shape is `within_own_footprint` at info: a single plain-pad opening (not a merged region) overlapping only the same-net pad(s) of its own footprint, every owner and the exposed pad on one identical non-empty net. JLCDFM located by position at that pad array (#9420, 2026-11-18, one board, one export setting): the two 0.19 mm pad pairs are Good under Pad spacing (Danger 0.1 mm, Warning 0.15 mm); Soldermask bridge is empty board-wide (0 danger / 0 warning / 0 good); none of the 6 Solder mask opening exposing trace warnings is at the pads (nearest about 35 mm away); and the 19 Soldermask opening with multiple segments warnings are reinforce-wire objects (8 of the 15 top-side items located by position, 40 mm or more away; the other 11 by object type only). `tht_smd_spacing` (#8843) judges plated through-hole component pads plus, since #8914, vias whose drill is at least 1.0 mm (the fab classes a hole by size: the three top-side dangers kct missed on the #8914 board were all 1.3-1.42 mm wire-anchor vias). Since #8925 an anchor via is also judged against any exposed (untented) via annulus -- the fab's `smd` side counts a small exposed via pad (#8914 item 5); THT component pads are not paired with via annuli, and tented annuli are skipped (the fab's exact tenting test is unverified). Since #9325 a same-net pair of anchor-sized vias is exempt (the fab counted none of the `kct pcb reinforce` anchor pairs on the #9325 board -- one-board evidence, not a general fab-rule confirmation); a pair colliding on net 0 is not exempt (net 0 is the no-net sentinel every unconnected hole resolves to, not a shared net). Still skipped: same-footprint pad pairs and sub-1.0 mm fan-out vias as the hole side. A pad shape the rule cannot measure now reports `tht_smd_spacing_incomplete` at info instead of vanishing. `silkscreen_line_width` (every silk graphic primitive) and `silkscreen_text_thickness` (text) enforce JLCPCB's published >= 0.15 mm. Not covered: JLCDFM flags silk that meets that floor (#8844: 63 warnings on gerbers with no silk stroke below 0.150 mm). How JLCDFM selects the items it flags is unknown (#8943). Text height is a separate floor: JLCPCB publishes 1.0 mm (40 mil) minimum character height (pcb-capabilities, verified 2026-11-18) and `silkscreen_text_height` enforces it; a project may declare a smaller reference-designator height (`silkscreen_min_reference_height_mm`, >= 0.8 mm, #9448) which relaxes that floor for designators only and is reported by `kct readiness` as a declared deviation -- the fab's own limit is unchanged.
